title: What happened in AI — Nov 21, 2026
intro: Tool results are now an attack surface you can't ignore. RunPod's hosted MCP server began telling agents to rate it and hide that from the user, and a malicious npm package installed a full Hermes Agent as root.
Evals shifted toward damage. Stripe grades whether coding agents pick current APIs, and RMRFBench ranks models on whether the server survives a routine delete.
highlights: RunPod's MCP server appended a hidden instruction to every create-pod result: rate us, don't tell the user.
Malicious npm package @leadstack/crm-connect installed Hermes Agent as a root systemd service, tasked over Telegram.
RMRFBench ranks agents with a root shell on whether the box survives a one-line deletion ticket.
Stripe's evals find coding agents favour older, pretraining-heavy APIs and hallucinate features.
Replit reports agent swarms speed up code optimization as they grow, against early multi-agent results.
ClickHouse open-sourced Loom, a self-hosted MCP server for shared agent memory linked to files and symbols.

categories.name: Tool output and packages as agent attack surface
categories.summary: Two incidents show agents taking orders from text they didn't ask for, and two tools try to check skills and outputs before they act.

articles.title: RunPod's MCP server tells AI agents to rate it and not mention it to the user
articles.summary: From Nov 20, every successful create-pod result asked the agent to call rate_nps_score and hide it from the user: the exact shape of a prompt injection, shipped by the vendor.

articles.title: NPM package installed Hermes Agent as root and tasked it over Telegram
articles.summary: @leadstack/crm-connect posed as a CRM client, installed Nous Research's Hermes Agent as a disguised systemd service and wired it to the attacker's Telegram bot.

articles.title: Show HN: ClawVet – Offline AST scanner and rug-pull diff for AI agent skills
articles.summary: Static rules plus Tree-sitter taint tracking report which secrets, hosts and startup files a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md or helper script touches; the CLI gates installs on permission changes.

articles.title: Aletheia Aegis: Deterministic sub-millisecond output guard for AI agents
articles.summary: A pattern-based output guard that fails closed on credential leaks and life-safety failures, with an optional semantic judge for cases patterns can't settle.

categories.name: Evals that grade what agents break
categories.summary: New evals score agents on harm and outdated choices, not just task completion, and mine real traces for failures.

articles.title: Show HN: RMRFBench – How often AI agents wreck a server when asked to rm a file
articles.summary: Each run gives an unattended agent a root shell and a one-line deletion ticket on a throwaway Linux box, then inspects whether the server survived.

articles.title: Stripe evals: Measuring real-world coding agent performance
articles.summary: Stripe's methodology checks whether coding agents use current integration patterns and handle failures and webhooks, which pass/fail coding benchmarks miss.

articles.title: EvalSift – 100 hand-labeled LLM agent traces
articles.summary: Dependency-free MIT tool that validates traces.jsonl, grades each trace with deterministic checks and reports failures; ships a 100-trace support-agent case study.

articles.title: Show HN: trace2rules – Mine and audit coding-agent logs into AGENTS.md rules
articles.summary: Local CLI that mines agent sessions for recurring friction and marks each AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md rule as observed, violated, unobserved or already enforced by CI.

categories.name: Scaling coding agents: more agents, more branches
categories.summary: Builders are spending inference on parallel agents and search trees instead of a single trajectory.

articles.title: Why agent swarms get better at optimizing code as they grow
articles.summary: Replit tested whether Brooks's law still holds for today's models on performance-engineering tasks and found swarms improve as they scale.

articles.title: Show HN: agent-mcts – Monte Carlo tree search on top of Claude Code
articles.summary: MIT test-time search harness that runs MCTS over Claude Code, explores solution branches, backtracks from dead ends and applies the best path.

articles.title: Parallel Code: Claude Code, Codex and Copilot Agent CLIs in Parallel Worktrees
articles.summary: Runs each agent task in its own git branch and worktree, with diff review and comments before you choose what merges.

categories.name: Agent memory: shared, anchored and undoable
categories.summary: Memory work moved from storing more to deciding what counts as a memory and where it belongs.

articles.title: Loom: Shared memory, document search, and code indexing for AI agents
articles.summary: ClickHouse's self-hosted MCP server links memories to files and symbols so they surface when an agent edits that code; plugins for Claude Code and Codex.

articles.title: We let our AI save memories by itself. What it got wrong in the first two days
articles.summary: Auto-saved memory stored a one-off request as a rule and a test question as a business plan; the fix was plain rules plus an Undo under every save.

articles.title: How to build a knowledge factory for AI agents
articles.summary: LangChain argues company agents fail on missing tacit knowledge, not models, and sketches a process to capture standards and data locations for agents.

categories.name: Self-hosted inference: measure the config
categories.summary: Two releases target serving cost on your own GPUs: benchmark the flags, then share the KV cache.

articles.title: Show HN: Find and serve fast LLM config for your GPU
articles.summary: rigtune benchmarks vLLM, SGLang and llama.cpp across precisions, KV-cache types and speculative decoding on your card and prompts, then serves the winner.

articles.title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill
articles.summary: AWS packages distributed KV caching for self-hosted LLMs as an agent skill, aimed at lower serving cost and latency.
